source.work: Hexagonal architecture (A. Cockburn; ports and adapters)
source.paraphrase: The application speaks to the outside through ports it owns. Adapters sit outside and may depend inward. The inside does not mention the adapter.

invariants.why: A domain or application module that names an adapter compiles only when that adapter is present, so the policy can no longer be tested or reused on its own.
invariants.fixHint: Depend on a port declared beside the domain, implement it in the adapter, and pass the implementation in from the composition root.
invariants.avoid: Hiding the same path behind export * or import(). A string that merely mentions the folder, and is not an import specifier, is not this edge.

source.paraphrase: A port is the shape the inside needs. The body that talks to a database, a network, or a framework is an adapter and lives outside.

invariants.why: An implementation in the port folder pulls a concrete dependency into the boundary the domain is allowed to import.
invariants.fixHint: Leave an interface or type alias in the port module. Move the class or function to an adapter that implements the port.
invariants.avoid: Marking the class abstract, or binding the body to an exported const arrow, still leaves an implementation in the port module.

source.work: Hexagonal architecture (A. Cockburn; ports and adapters)
source.locator: driving adapter to driven adapter boundary
source.paraphrase: Input/driving adapters speak to the application core through input ports; they do not reach directly into output/driven adapters, bypassing the center.

invariants.why: Direct communication between adapters bypasses domain logic, use-case orchestration, and port contracts.
invariants.fixHint: Dispatch the request through an application use case or input port, and let the use case call the output port.
invariants.avoid: Importing repositories or secondary adapters directly into HTTP controllers or queue consumers.

relations.why: Both flag crypto randomness and performance.now() when domain, entity, or use-case folders belong to the core layer.
relations.settle: Keep one active or turn architecture/ARCH-EFF-002 off when FCIS-IO-002 covers the core layer.

source.work: Hexagonal architecture (A. Cockburn; ports and adapters) and Grokking Simplicity (E. Normand, 2021)
source.locator: driven ports for nondeterministic clock and ID generation
source.paraphrase: Domain entities and application use cases receive identifiers and timestamps through explicit inputs or driven ports instead of calling Web Crypto or high-resolution timers directly.

invariants.why: Direct calls to crypto.randomUUID(), crypto.getRandomValues(), or performance.now() make domain and use-case logic non-deterministic and impossible to replay deterministically in unit tests.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the generated identifier, random bytes, or timestamp as a parameter from an adapter or inject a narrow Clock / IdGenerator port.
invariants.avoid: Qualifying the call with globalThis or window in domain, entities, or use-cases directories still couples core logic to ambient runtime effects.
